name: Medial Epicondylitis (Golfer's Elbow) Rehabilitation Protocol
description: Evidence-based protocol for medial elbow tendinopathy using isometric and heavy-slow resistance training with emphasis on wrist flexors and pronators
pain_rule: Pain max. 3/10 during the exercise. Avoid painful gripping and twisting movements in daily life.
evidence_base: Clinical Practice Guidelines for Lateral Elbow Pain (JOSPT 2022) - principles applicable to medial epicondylitis
Heavy-Slow Resistance Training: Kongsgaard et al. (2009) - superior long-term outcomes for tendinopathy
Isometric Loading: Rio et al. (2015) - pain reduction without aggravating tendinopathy
Load Management: Cook & Purdam (2009) - progressive loading essential for tendon adaptation
progression_criteria: All sets/reps completed without increase in pain
No morning stiffness in the elbow

exercises.name: Isometric Wrist Flexion
exercises.description: Sitting with forearm supported on table (palm up), wrist in neutral position
exercises.phase_goal: Reduce pain and begin tendon loading without aggravation

exercises.name: Isometric Pronation
exercises.description: Elbow at 90°, forearm neutral, resisting pronation (turning palm down)
exercises.phase_goal: Reduce pain and begin tendon loading without aggravation

exercises.name: Wrist Flexion (Dumbbell)
exercises.description: Forearm supported on table, palm up, wrist extending over edge. Curl dumbbell up and down with controlled tempo
exercises.phase_goal: Build tendon strength and capacity through progressive loading

exercises.name: Pronation (Hammer/Dumbbell)
exercises.description: Elbow supported at 90°, holding hammer or dumbbell vertically. Rotate from supination to pronation
exercises.phase_goal: Build tendon strength and capacity through progressive loading

exercises.name: Eccentric Wrist Flexion
exercises.description: Palm up, wrist extending over table edge. Lower weight slowly over 4 seconds, lift with other hand
exercises.phase_goal: Build tendon strength and capacity through progressive loading

exercises.name: Resisted Grip Strengthening
exercises.description: Forearm supported, squeezing therapy putty or gripper with controlled tempo
exercises.phase_goal: Build tendon strength and capacity through progressive loading
